key_insight: Applying economic theory and incentive design to AI development reframes AI as a set of economic actors and public goods, enabling concrete mechanisms to align AI outcomes with the common good. This shifts focus from purely technical fixes to incentive, governance and evaluation structures that shape system behavior at scale.
problem_solved: Addresses misaligned incentives and market failures (externalities, concentration, under-provision of public goods) that lead AI deployment to harm social welfare despite technical progress.
method: Map AI systems and stakeholders to economic models (public goods, externalities, principal–agent problems) to identify failure modes.
Propose incentive and mechanism-design interventions (pricing, regulation, funding structures, reward redesign) to internalize social costs and promote equitable provision of AI benefits.
Illustrate policy and governance pathways by combining normative objectives with measurable economic metrics for deployment and evaluation.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners, designers and policymakers a practical framework to anticipate incentive-driven harms and embed economic levers that steer systems toward broader social benefit. This makes deployment decisions, evaluation metrics and governance choices more actionable and accountable.
visual_elements: Sankey-style diagram showing flows of incentives, benefits and harms between AI developers, users, platforms and society.
2×2 matrix classifying AI outcomes by private benefit vs. social welfare (public good, common resource, private good, negative externality).
Mechanism-design flowchart: problem → economic framing → intervention (pricing/regulation/funding) → measurable outcomes.
Bar/line chart comparing baseline vs. intervention metrics (e.g., social welfare, concentration, access) to show impact of economic levers.
paper_title: AI economics for the common good
